feature_results.rationale: The official hooks reference documents user-defined command handlers around tool execution, including PreToolUse and PostToolUse. A worked example reads tool input and returns permissionDecision deny to block the action. This is an active lifecycle extension mechanism, not merely a passive notification webhook.

evidence.excerpt: Hooks are user-defined shell commands, HTTP endpoints, MCP tool calls, LLM prompts, or subagents that execute automatically at specific points in Claude Code's lifecycle.
Claude Code reads the JSON decision, blocks the tool call, and shows Claude the reason.

constraints.description: PreToolUse and PostToolUse fire around tool calls except EndConversation, which skips both events.
Cloud sessions do not read local user settings from ~/.claude/settings.json; the hooks available there depend on the settings, plugins, and managed sources that reach the cloud environment.

queries: GET https://code.claude.com/docs/en/overview (known source; followed its Hooks navigation link)
GET https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks (first 18000 characters; lifecycle, decision example, and hook locations)

feature_results.rationale: The built-in shell sandbox routes outbound connections through a host-checking proxy, with configurable allowed and denied domains. This is a network-specific enforced boundary, not merely process isolation. Anthropic-hosted cloud sessions also document configurable disabled or domain-allowlisted network access.

evidence.excerpt: No direct route out. Connections go through a proxy on your machine that checks each host against your allowed domains, which start empty.
[`network.allowedDomains`](/docs/en/settings-reference#sandbox-network-alloweddomains), [`network.deniedDomains`](/docs/en/settings-reference#sandbox-network-denieddomains)
Network access is limited by default and can be configured to be disabled or allow only specific domains

constraints.description: Local shell sandboxing runs on macOS, Linux, and WSL2, but not native Windows. Linux and WSL2 require bubblewrap and socat.

The local sandbox is off by default and covers shell commands and descendants, not built-in file/web tools, hooks, or MCP servers. Excluded commands and approved unsandboxed retries can bypass it; administrators can disable retries and fail startup if sandboxing is unavailable.
Anthropic-hosted cloud network controls are distinct from self-hosted environments, whose egress enforcement is the customer's responsibility.

queries: GET https://code.claude.com/docs/en/overview (known source reused before searches)

feature_results.rationale: The /rewind menu restores tracked code changes across the session and its conversation to a selected earlier prompt in one operation. This is session-wide rollback, not per-file or per-hunk review. It does not restore every possible side effect: shell modifications and most subagent edits are excluded.

evidence.excerpt: As you work with Claude, checkpointing automatically captures the state of your code before each prompt you send that starts a turn.
**Restore code and conversation**: revert both code and conversation to that point

constraints.description: Only changes captured by the file-editing tools are tracked. Bash modifications, most subagent edits, and external changes are not restored; symlinked and hard-linked paths are skipped.
File snapshots are kept for the 100 most recent checkpoints. Default retention deletes session snapshots about 30 days after the session last saved one; retention is configurable.

feature_results.rationale: Administrators can centrally configure OpenTelemetry export of organizational usage metrics and per-event tool activity, including tool results and permission decisions, to their own collector. This exceeds aggregate-only dashboards and is not documented as an Enterprise-only logging feature. Team/Enterprise and API dashboards additionally provide organizational usage reporting; the Enterprise Analytics API is tier-restricted.

evidence.excerpt: Track Claude Code usage, costs, and tool activity across your organization by exporting telemetry data through OpenTelemetry (OTel).
Administrators can configure OpenTelemetry settings for all users through the [managed settings file](/docs/en/managed-settings#delivery-mechanisms).
Claude Code exports the following events via OpenTelemetry logs/events (when `OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER` is configured):
Navigate to [claude.ai/analytics/claude-code](https://claude.ai/analytics/claude-code). Admins and Owners can view the dashboard.
[OpenTelemetry export](/docs/en/monitoring-usage) works on every setup and is the only option that streams per-user token and cost metrics into your own observability stack in near real time.

constraints.description: Organizational event export requires enabling telemetry and configuring a logs exporter and reachable collector. Customer-operated export is not a promise of a vendor-hosted immutable audit archive.

Team and Enterprise provide admin dashboards; the Enterprise Analytics API is not available on Team. Console API customers have a separate dashboard and Claude Code Analytics API. Cloud-provider usage requires OpenTelemetry or a gateway rather than Anthropic dashboards.

Prompts and tool details are redacted by default and require explicit content-logging settings to include. Cloud sessions need telemetry configuration reaching their cloud environment; local device settings alone do not configure them.

queries: GET https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs (known source, including organization reporting section)
GET https://code.claude.com/docs/en/monitoring-usage (initial section and ranges starting at 32000 and 63000)

feature_results.rationale: Claude Code documents a dedicated managed GitHub PR review workflow that automatically analyzes changes and posts inline findings. This satisfies the hosting-integrated criterion rather than merely local diff review. Other plans can use a dedicated local /code-review command, and CI alternatives are documented separately.

evidence.excerpt: Code Review analyzes your GitHub pull requests and posts findings as inline comments on the lines of code where it found issues.
Once an Owner enables Code Review for your organization, reviews trigger when a PR opens, on every push, or when manually requested, depending on the repository's configured behavior.

constraints.description: Managed Code Review is available to Team and Enterprise subscriptions; organizations with Zero Data Retention or HIPAA configuration cannot use it, and it is not covered by Anthropic's BAA.
Managed Code Review is in research preview.
An organization Owner must enable the service, install the Claude GitHub App, and grant repository access.
Reviews do not approve or block merging. Fork PRs require an authorized comment command and are not automatically reviewed on creation or subsequent pushes.

feature_results.rationale: Official workflows document AI-driven modernization of a file while maintaining behavior, including identifying deprecated APIs, proposing structural changes, applying the refactor, and testing it. This is broader than a single-symbol rename and does not depend on a manual IDE refactor command. The overview confirms that the coding engine can coordinate work across multiple files.

evidence.excerpt: refactor utils.js to use ES2024 features while maintaining the same behavior
It understands your entire codebase and can work across multiple files and tools to get things done.

constraints.description: Behavior preservation is an instructed objective, not a formal guarantee; the documented workflow explicitly follows the refactor with tests and recommends small, testable increments.

feature_results.rationale: The official test workflow explicitly generates scaffolding and edge-case tests for specified existing code, examines existing tests to follow the project's framework and assertion conventions, and runs and fixes the generated tests. No small fixed framework or language set is stated in this workflow.

evidence.excerpt: Claude can generate tests that follow your project's existing patterns and conventions.
Claude examines your existing test files to match the style, frameworks, and assertion patterns already in use.
claude "write tests for the auth module, run them, and fix any failures"

feature_results.rationale: Claude Code decomposes tasks, chooses tools, chains edits and commands, verifies results, and adjusts its approach in an agentic loop. Auto mode and cloud routines provide execution without routine step-by-step confirmation; autonomy is not limited to fixed workflows.

evidence.excerpt: For complex tasks, it breaks work into steps, executes them, and adjusts based on what it learns.
Claude decides what each step requires based on what it learned from the previous step, chaining dozens of actions together and course-correcting along the way.

Runs without routine prompts; before actions such as shell commands and network requests run, a background [classifier](/docs/en/permission-modes#eliminate-prompts-with-auto-mode) checks that they align with your request

constraints.description: Manual mode requires approval for shell commands except built-in read-only commands. Allow rules or other permission modes change the confirmation model; managed settings can disable auto mode.
The agent remains interruptible and can ask questions; autonomy does not guarantee completion without any user input.

queries: GET https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions (initial content and continuation at character 9700)

feature_results.rationale: Agent view dispatches full Claude Code sessions that continue without an attached terminal while the user does other work. It sends completion or failure notifications through the configured terminal channel while agent view is open. Cloud sessions additionally continue after the user's laptop closes.

evidence.excerpt: Each background session is a full Claude Code conversation that keeps running without a terminal attached, so you can open it, reply, and leave whenever you want.

While agent view is open, Claude Code also sends a notification through your configured [terminal notification channel](/docs/en/terminal-config#get-a-terminal-bell-or-notification) when a local background session starts needing your input, finishes, or fails.
The session keeps running after you close your laptop, and you can check on it or steer it from any device.

constraints.description: Agent view is in research preview.
Local background sessions survive terminal closure and sleep but shutdown stops running sessions. Scheduled /loop sessions notify only when they need user input.
Cloud sessions require Pro, Max, Team, or Enterprise premium seats or Chat + Claude Code seats, and count against plan usage limits.

feature_results.rationale: Official workflows document natural-language requests to find code, but do not establish repository-wide meaning-based retrieval ranked by relevance. Current large-codebase and code-intelligence documentation describes grep/file reads and LSP symbol navigation, neither of which alone qualifies. Scoped searches did not establish an embedding or other semantic retrieval integration. The connector directory did not expose its catalog and only part of the large official marketplace catalog was accessed, so an integration may remain undiscovered. The negative protocol is incomplete; not_found would be unjustified.

evidence.excerpt: Claude gets an LSP tool that looks up symbols through the server instead of searching text for them.
In a large codebase, finding where a symbol is defined or used can cost many file reads and grep calls.

queries: semantic search, embeddings, code search, and dependency/CVE scanning in Claude Code or Anthropic integration catalog site:code.claude.com OR site:claude.com OR site:github.com/anthropics
site:code.claude.com semantic search documentation embedding index relevance-ranked natural-language retrieval
site:github.com/anthropics/claude-plugins-official semantic search documentation embedding index retrieval plugin
access_gaps: https://claude.ai/directory returned an HTML application shell, not usable connector listings.
https://claude.com/marketplace/plugins returned only a Supabase description, not the full searchable catalog.
The official marketplace JSON and changelog were only partially accessed; complete integration and historical coverage was not established.

feature_results.rationale: Users can author Markdown subagent definitions with YAML frontmatter or supply --agents JSON. The Markdown body supplies the system prompt, tools/disallowedTools independently scope access, and permissionMode and mcpServers provide additional per-agent configuration. Project and user definitions are documented supported mechanisms.

evidence.excerpt: Each subagent runs in its own context window with a custom system prompt, specific tool access, and independent permissions.
Subagent files use YAML frontmatter for configuration, followed by the system prompt in Markdown:
Beyond these built-in subagents, you can create your own with custom prompts, tool restrictions, permission modes, hooks, and skills.

constraints.description: Plugin-loaded subagent definitions ignore hooks, mcpServers, and permissionMode frontmatter. To use these per-agent fields, copy the definition into project or user agents directories; tool scoping remains documented.

If the agents directory did not exist when the session started, its first new definition requires a restart. Existing watched project and user agents directories support definition updates without restarting.

queries: GET https://code.claude.com/docs/en/overview (known source; followed custom agents navigation)
GET https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents (characters 0-36000 across two fetches; creation, scopes, CLI definitions, and frontmatter)

feature_results.rationale: The documented native mods API exposes $.tool.register with a name, description, and input JSON Schema, and a JavaScript tool.call handler implements the callable tool in Claude Code's process. Although the exposed tool name uses the mcp__ prefix and supports MCP tool deferral, this mechanism does not require registering or running an MCP server. It therefore meets the non-MCP registration criterion rather than relying on the excluded MCP-only integration or SDK in-process MCP server pattern.

evidence.excerpt: A tool is for Claude. Register it with a name, a description Claude reads, and a JSON Schema for its input.
await $.tool.register({
A mod's handlers are functions that run inside Claude Code instead.
When you ask about a ticket, Claude can call `mcp__my-mod__ticket` with its id. The second hook fetches the ticket and returns the response body, which Claude reads as the tool's result.

constraints.description: The native registration surface is delivered by a plugin containing a mod, with registration during session.start and execution handled by a tool.call hook.

The mods overview specifies Claude Code v2.1.287 or later in the terminal, and v2.1.286 for the Desktop app's bundled engine. These are documented mods availability minimums, not a claim about the first historical tool-registration release.
Mod hooks run in sessions that load the plugin, including CLI, VS Code, non-interactive/SDK, and supported cloud sessions. Desktop WSL sessions do not run them because plugins are unavailable there.
Mods run with the user's permissions and are not sandboxed; users or managed organization settings can prevent installed mods from loading.

GET https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anthropics/claude-code/main/CHANGELOG.md (known source; first 12000 characters, references to mods)

GET https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/mods/api (first 16000 characters; Add a tool section)

feature_results.rationale: Anthropic publishes a concrete Data Processing Addendum and incorporates it into its electronically accepted Commercial Terms. Claude Code documentation explicitly identifies Team, Enterprise, and API use as governed by those terms. Availability is therefore not limited to a specially negotiated Enterprise tier; consumer-plan coverage should not be inferred.

evidence.excerpt: Data submitted through the Services will be processed in accordance with the [Anthropic Data Processing Addendum](https://www.anthropic.com/legal/data-processing-addendum) (“**DPA**”), which is incorporated into these Terms by reference.
This Data Processing Addendum (**“DPA”**) is incorporated into and forms part of the Anthropic Commercial Terms of Service or other agreement between Customer and Anthropic that references this DPA
[Commercial Terms of Service](https://www.anthropic.com/legal/commercial-terms) (for Team, Enterprise, and API users)

constraints.description: The publicly incorporated DPA covers commercial-contract use, including Team, Enterprise, and API. Free, Pro, and Max use consumer terms instead; separate DPA availability for those tiers is not established.

Acceptance is through the incorporating commercial agreement, not a documented requirement to separately countersign the public DPA. Third-party features are outside Anthropic's Services under these terms.

queries: Find official Anthropic documentation on Claude Code data residency region selection inference_geo ANTHROPIC_INFERENCE_GEO and customer Data Processing Addendum DPA availability and generated code copyright indemnification.

feature_results.rationale: Claude Code supports API-backed organizational use, where Anthropic's workspace controls enforce allowed inference geographies and a default geography on requests using that workspace's keys. Customers can restrict model inference to US infrastructure rather than global routing, while workspace geo governs storage and endpoint processing. This establishes a constrained API deployment capability, not a blanket residency guarantee for all claude.ai subscription or cloud-session data.

evidence.excerpt: **`allowed_inference_geos`:** Restricts which geos a workspace can use. If a request specifies an `inference_geo` not in this list, the API returns an error.
Workspace geo is set when you create a workspace and can't be changed afterward. Currently, `"us"` is the only available workspace geo.
All API requests using keys from your workspace continue to run on US-based infrastructure.
API organizations manage Claude Code spend through [workspaces](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/workspaces).

constraints.description: The evidenced first-party region control is the Claude API workspace mechanism. Amazon Bedrock and Google Cloud use endpoint or inference-profile geography instead, and Foundry has deployment-specific geography rather than inference_geo.
Inference geo currently supports only us and global; workspace geo supports only us. This is not evidence of a selectable EU first-party residency region.
inference_geo is supported on Claude 4.6 and later models; earlier models reject requests carrying the parameter.
US-only inference costs 1.1 times standard token rates on supported first-party API models. No subscription-wide regional residency guarantee is asserted.

Workspace geo controls at-rest data and endpoint processing separately from model inference. Model-region restrictions alone should not be interpreted as a restriction on every telemetry, feedback, or cloud-session data flow.

queries: GET https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs (known source reused, including data-residency billing and workspaces)

Find official Anthropic documentation on Claude Code data residency region selection inference_geo ANTHROPIC_INFERENCE_GEO and customer Data Processing Addendum DPA availability and generated code copyright indemnification.
GET https://code.claude.com/docs/en/env-vars (initial section and range starting at 17000; no inference-geo environment variable claimed)

feature_results.rationale: Consumer accounts have an actionable privacy preference controlling model-improvement use, explicitly covering Claude Code. Switching it off also changes the stated server retention from five years to thirty days. Commercial Claude Code use is not used to train generative models by default unless the customer opts in. Qualified Enterprise organizations can request ZDR, while local transcript retention has a separate configurable cleanup period.

evidence.excerpt: We will train new models using data from Free, Pro, and Max accounts when this setting is on (including when you use Claude Code from these accounts).
Users who don't allow data use for model improvement: 30-day retention period
Privacy settings can be changed at any time at [claude.ai/settings/data-privacy-controls](https://claude.ai/settings/data-privacy-controls).
Consumer users can change their [privacy settings](https://claude.ai/settings/privacy) at any time.

constraints.description: Training opt-out is actionable on consumer plans, so the feature is not Enterprise-only. ZDR is separate, available to qualified Claude for Enterprise organizations through their account team and not included automatically in the standard Enterprise plan.

Training opt-out is not zero retention: consumer opt-out retains data for thirty days. Local session transcripts are plaintext and retained thirty days by default, adjustable with cleanupPeriodDays; Desktop/Cowork transcripts have documented default exceptions.

Voluntarily shared feedback transcripts have separate retention, including five years for feedback-command reports; model-training preferences should not be read as disabling every feedback or telemetry flow.

feature_results.rationale: Dependency scanning is available through the documented Snyk MCP integration, not asserted as a built-in Claude scanner. Anthropic's connector catalog explicitly lists SCA and snyk_sca_scan; Snyk's own Claude Code guide confirms that this tool inspects dependency manifests and queries the Snyk vulnerability database. This directly satisfies the integration-based has criterion. LLM security review alone was not used to substantiate CVE/database matching.

evidence.excerpt: Detect vulnerabilities in open source dependencies

Analyzes Projects for open-source vulnerabilities and license compliance issues by inspecting manifest files (for example package.json, pom.xml, requirements.txt) to understand dependencies and then queries the Snyk vulnerability database.
Obtain Snyk security findings directly in your MCP-enabled tool or environment.

constraints.description: Requires installing/configuring Snyk Studio or Snyk CLI's MCP server for Claude Code; the guide exposes authentication and folder-trust tools.
SCA may execute ecosystem tools such as Gradle or Maven to fetch dependency trees; scanning relies on the Snyk integration rather than native Claude vulnerability-database matching.

queries: semantic search, embeddings, code search, and dependency/CVE scanning in Claude Code or Anthropic integration catalog site:code.claude.com OR site:claude.com OR site:github.com/anthropics

Find first-party Anthropic pages documenting Claude Code integration with Snyk or Socket or OSV for dependency CVE vulnerability scanning. Search specifically site:claude.com/connectors snyk socket and site:github.com/anthropics/claude-plugins-official snyk socket. Return actual official URLs, not inferred capabilities.
Snyk MCP Claude Code integration official documentation scanning dependencies

feature_results.rationale: The VS Code extension in Manual mode shows original and proposed content before asking permission to edit. Users can accept or reject individual changes, edit the proposal, and then finish the whole-file review. This satisfies both pre-write review and selective application, rather than merely showing a post-edit diff.

evidence.excerpt: In Manual mode, when Claude wants to edit a file, it shows a side-by-side comparison of the original and proposed changes, then asks for permission. You can accept, reject, or tell Claude what to do instead.
To review a proposed edit one change at a time, use the **Accept this change** and **Reject this change** buttons under each change in the diff.

constraints.description: The verified per-change controls are documented for the VS Code extension, which requires VS Code 1.94.0 or later.
Per-change review requires Claude Code v2.1.275 or later. Diffs with more than 100 changes omit per-change buttons and must be reviewed at whole-file granularity.
Use Manual permission mode for pre-write approval. Auto and Edit automatically modes edit most workspace files without asking.
The extension requires a paid Claude subscription or Claude Console account; third-party provider access is also documented.

feature_results.rationale: Claude Code's data-usage documentation explicitly states TLS 1.2+ encryption for prompts and outputs in transit and AES-256 infrastructure-level disk encryption at rest for the Anthropic API. These concrete customer-data statements meet both parts of the criteria. They do not imply local client transcripts are encrypted.

evidence.excerpt: This data includes all user prompts and model outputs, encrypted in transit via TLS 1.2+.
| Anthropic API | Infrastructure-level disk encryption (AES-256).

constraints.description: At-rest encryption depends on provider. The Anthropic API documents AES-256 disk encryption; Bedrock documents AES-256 and optional customer-managed KMS keys, Google Cloud documents managed keys and CMEK, and Foundry depends on hosting option.
Claude Code local session transcripts are stored in plaintext. Vendor-side encryption is not a promise of encrypted local transcripts or end-to-end encryption.

feature_results.rationale: Claude Code documents Team SSO and Enterprise role-based permissions, as well as Console SSO and role assignment. The official SSO setup guide applies to Team, Enterprise, and Console organizations and links SAML configurations for multiple identity providers. This establishes SSO plus organizational role/permission management rather than only individual authentication.

evidence.excerpt: **Claude for Enterprise**: adds domain capture, role-based permissions, and the compliance API.
**Claude Code** role: users can only create Claude Code API keys
Single sign-on is available for Team plans, Enterprise plans, and Console organizations.
Okta SAML

constraints.description: Team supports SSO and team administration; Enterprise explicitly adds role-based permissions and domain capture. Console has separate role and SSO setup.
SSO setup requires company-domain verification and access to the identity provider. WorkOS handles verification/setup. Multiple domains within an organization must use one IdP.

Team/Enterprise SSO configuration requires Owner or Primary Owner; Console requires Admin. Requiring SSO is an explicit enforcement toggle after setup, and Console identity settings require sales enablement or a completed merge proposal.

feature_results.rationale: No documented full or partial zero-network mode was found. The current system requirements explicitly require an internet connection, and enterprise networking documents API and authentication endpoints. Local execution, private-network gateways, and self-hosted runners do not establish offline inference or whole-product offline operation. Cloud work continuing after the user disconnects means the remote service remains online. Search summaries claiming offline operation via substitute local models were not accepted as evidence: the official gateway documentation explicitly does not support non-Claude models, and model substitution alone is excluded by this feature definition. Relevant official source classes were checked; no material access gap or unresolved official-source conflict remained.

constraints.description: An internet connection is a documented system requirement; disabling optional telemetry is not a zero-network operating mode.

queries: Search official Claude Code documentation and Anthropic release notes for full offline or air-gapped zero-network operation. Check whether internet access remains required for inference, distinguishing running locally and cloud tasks continuing after a client disconnects. Prioritize code.claude.com/docs/en/setup, network-config and anthropics/claude-code CHANGELOG.

Find official first-party pages only (code.claude.com, claude.com, anthropic.com, github.com/anthropics/claude-code) explicitly documenting or denying Claude Code fully offline operation, air-gapped zero network, or local models. Do not treat third-party local-model wrappers or AWS private network inference as zero-network operation. Include any official changelog entries about offline mode.

feature_results.rationale: The official overview documents direct Git operation: staging changes, writing commit messages, creating branches, and opening pull requests. This is execution within Claude Code, not merely suggested commands for the user.

evidence.excerpt: Claude Code works directly with git. It stages changes, writes commit messages, creates branches, and opens pull requests.

feature_results.rationale: The CLI's print mode runs non-interactively, supports auto-approved tool allowlists, JSON and streaming JSON output, and documented success/failure exit semantics. The programmatic guide explicitly targets scripts and CI/CD. Authentication and appropriate permissions must be provisioned before unattended execution.

evidence.excerpt: Add the `-p` (or `--print`) flag to any `claude` command to run it non-interactively.
Claude Code exits with code 0 on success and a non-zero code when the run fails, so your scripts can branch on the exit status.
`json`: structured JSON with result, session ID, and metadata
Tools that execute without prompting for permission, apart from reads from [network paths](/docs/en/permissions#network-paths).

constraints.description: Use -p with an appropriate allowedTools configuration for unattended tool execution. Network-path reads are an exception to the no-prompt allowedTools behavior.
Bare mode does not read subscription OAuth credentials or the system keychain; supply an Anthropic API key/apiKeyHelper or third-party provider credentials.

feature_results.rationale: No verified official page accessed in this task confirms ambient, as-you-type code-editor ghost text. The IDE pages describe explicitly prompted assistance, diffs, and selection sharing. Interactive-mode autocomplete is in the prompt input and file-path mentions, so it is excluded. The search summary asserted absence but largely cited third-party material and cannot substantiate a feature status. Exhaustive negative coverage was not completed, so absence is not claimed.

evidence.excerpt: While autocomplete suggestions are showing in the prompt input, accepts the selected suggestion.
Ask Claude to help with your code or files, whether that's explaining how something works, debugging an issue, or making changes.

queries: Find official Anthropic Claude Code documentation or announcements about as-you-type inline code completion or ghost-text suggestions inside the code editor (not prompt suggestions, file-path autocomplete, or inline diffs). Search code.claude.com and claude.com for whether Claude Code supports this feature.
access_gaps: The full long changelog, remaining VS Code documentation, remaining interactive-mode reference, and remaining specialist article were not inspected. Only fetched sections were checked; comprehensive negative coverage is incomplete.
The web search did not surface a directly verified official statement confirming or denying code-editor inline completion.

feature_results.rationale: The Commercial Terms explicitly provide defense and indemnification for third-party IP claims involving authorized paid Services use or its generated Outputs, and Claude Code identifies Team, Enterprise, and API users as subject to those terms. This is a concrete indemnity commitment, but only the indemnity branch is confirmed; no configurable public-code duplication filter is established in the pages checked. The input's partial criterion for only one confirmed component takes precedence over its overlapping has wording.

evidence.excerpt: Anthropic will defend Customer and its personnel, successors, and assigns from and against any Customer Claim
Outputs generated through such authorized use violates any third-party intellectual property right.
[Commercial Terms of Service](https://www.anthropic.com/legal/commercial-terms) (for Team, Enterprise, and API users)

constraints.description: Indemnity is for authorized paid use under Commercial Terms; consumer Pro/Max paid subscriptions should not be assumed covered by this commercial clause. Claude Code links these terms for Team, Enterprise, and API users.

The clause has material exclusions, including customer modifications, combinations with non-Anthropic technology/content, customer Inputs, knowingly infringing use, patented inventions in Outputs, and trademark use in commerce; claim notice and cooperation requirements also apply.
Only indemnification is positively confirmed. The partial result does not claim an exhaustive negative finding for a duplication filter.

queries: Find official Anthropic documentation on Claude Code data residency region selection inference_geo ANTHROPIC_INFERENCE_GEO and customer Data Processing Addendum DPA availability and generated code copyright indemnification.

feature_results.rationale: Managed organization, personal user, shared project, and local project instruction scopes load automatically in documented order. However, the documentation explicitly says instructions are concatenated rather than overridden and that conflicting user and project rules may follow either one. Thus this is layered loading without a defined conflict-precedence hierarchy, matching partial rather than has. Enforced settings precedence is distinct and was not substituted for custom-instruction precedence.

evidence.excerpt: All discovered files are concatenated into context rather than overriding each other.

Claude Code loads user-level rules before project rules, so a project rule appears later in Claude's context than a user rule. Neither set overrides the other: if a user rule and a project rule conflict, Claude may follow either one, so keep the two consistent.

constraints.description: Load order is documented, but conflicting instructions are not resolved by guaranteed scope precedence. Managed settings enforce controls separately from behavioral CLAUDE.md guidance.

feature_results.rationale: No supported customer-controlled local or self-hosted inference backend was found. Current official gateway documentation explicitly excludes support for non-Claude models. Model configuration documents Claude model aliases and cloud-provider model identifiers, and distinguishes changing the request endpoint from changing the model. Self-hosted environments deploy session execution, not a local model: they still require Anthropic connectivity and use Anthropic or documented cloud-provider inference. Custom gateways and local CLI execution therefore do not meet this feature's criteria. Current documentation resolves the apparent ambiguity of configurable base URLs; no official confirmation of local model support was found in the checked product, integration, pricing, or release sources.

feature_results.rationale: Claude Code documents codebase-specific context management: on-demand nested project instructions, path-scoped rules, excluding irrelevant instructions and generated files, precise symbol navigation, and isolated subagent exploration that returns summaries. For long sessions it automatically compacts conversation history and supports custom compaction instructions. These are mechanisms for repository and task context, not merely a general model context-window size; they do not guarantee performance at a particular repository size.

use_cases.title: Generate tests and repair failures
use_cases.description: Add scaffolding and edge cases for existing code using the repository's test conventions, then run the generated tests and fix failures. The test framework and executable dependencies must be available.

evidence.excerpt: Claude examines your existing test files to match the style, frameworks, and assertion patterns already in use.
run the new tests and fix any failures

use_cases.title: Implement and verify a multi-file feature
use_cases.description: Describe a feature in natural language, let Claude Code coordinate implementation across files, and verify the change with available project tools. Review the result; vendor-described verification is not a correctness guarantee.

evidence.excerpt: Describe what you want in plain language. Claude Code plans the approach, writes the code across multiple files, and verifies it works.

use_cases.title: Implement an issue through MCP and open a PR
use_cases.description: Connect an issue-tracker MCP server so the agent can read requirements directly and implement the requested feature before creating a GitHub PR. This requires the appropriate connectors, repository access, and credentials; it is not a connector-free native Jira capability.

evidence.excerpt: Add the feature described in JIRA issue ENG-4521 and create a PR on GitHub.

use_cases.title: Explore an unfamiliar repository
use_cases.description: Ask for a repository overview, architecture patterns, key models, and an explanation of authentication flow. This is documented code exploration, not a claim that repository search uses embeddings or relevance-ranked semantic retrieval.

evidence.excerpt: give me an overview of this codebase
trace the login process from front-end to database

use_cases.title: Schedule repository maintenance
use_cases.description: Use cloud routines for recurring PR reviews, CI failure analysis, or dependency audits when the computer is off; use Desktop scheduling for tasks requiring local files and tools. Cloud routines are in research preview, and local Desktop tasks require an awake computer and open app. Vulnerability-database scanning requires a configured integration such as Snyk rather than an LLM review alone.

evidence.excerpt: Run Claude on a schedule to automate work that repeats: morning PR reviews, overnight CI failure analysis, weekly dependency audits, or syncing docs after PRs merge.
Tasks that should run even when your computer is off.

use_cases.title: Modernize legacy code with regression checks
use_cases.description: Locate deprecated APIs, request a behavior-preserving refactor, and run tests afterward. Work in small increments and verify compatibility instead of assuming the agent formally preserves behavior.

evidence.excerpt: refactor utils.js to use ES2024 features while maintaining the same behavior
Do refactoring in small, testable increments

release_history.summary: Introduced Claude Mods for deeper plugin customization and the opt-in You should know helper mod. Added MCP URL prompts and VS Code background controls alongside permission and reliability fixes.

evidence.excerpt: <Update label="2.1.287" description="October 1, 2026">
Added Claude Mods: plugins may now modify deeper behavior

release_history.summary: Added mod selection access, built-in gh api for cloud images lacking GitHub CLI, cleared-prompt recovery, expanded code-review finding limits, and agent-view search. Changed background command time limits to apply only to unattended sessions.

evidence.excerpt: <Update label="2.1.288" description="October 2, 2026">
Changed the background command time limit to apply only in unattended sessions (`-p`, Agent SDK, CI, cloud); terminal, desktop app and VS Code sessions have no limit

release_history.summary: Added teammate-spawn hooks and consistent agent IDs across plugin events, with idle and waiting states. Fixed permission enforcement and mod loading/rendering problems and reverted a sign-in status change associated with more frequent sign-outs.

evidence.excerpt: <Update label="2.1.289" description="October 3, 2026">
Added `agent.spawn` for teammates, one agent id across plugin hook events, and idle and waiting states in `$.agent.list()`

release_history.summary: Expanded mod permission metadata and session-name attachment commands; improved background scheduling and many permission, plugin, rendering, and resume paths. A cloud wakeup-recovery fix in this release was subsequently reverted in 2.1.293.

evidence.excerpt: <Update label="2.1.290" description="October 5, 2026">
Added `claude attach <name>` and `claude logs <name>`: part of a session name works in place of the id

release_history.summary: Fixed regressions that could drop cloud permission-prompt answers or lose the last messages when quitting a session.

evidence.excerpt: <Update label="2.1.291" description="October 6, 2026">
Fixed a regression in 2.1.290 where cloud sessions could drop answers to permission prompts
Fixed a regression in 2.1.288 where the last messages of a session could be lost when quitting

release_history.summary: Added marketplace-aware plugin installation, per-Agent-call effort, mod prompt autocomplete, and prompt caching for mod model calls. Included fixes for sandbox read protection, managed settings, permission checks, and scheduled-task persistence.

evidence.excerpt: <Update label="2.1.292" description="October 6, 2026">
Added an `effort` parameter to the Agent tool, so Claude runs a sub-agent at the effort level you ask for

release_history.summary: Added Claude Haiku 5.5, subagent type metadata, and an option to expose mod-tool schemas immediately rather than defer them. Reverted an earlier cloud scheduling recovery fix, so that historical fix should not be described as universally current.

evidence.excerpt: <Update label="2.1.293" description="October 7, 2026">
Added `isDeferred` to `$.tool.register` for mods: `false` lists the tool's schema in the prompt from the start instead of behind tool search
Reverted the 2.1.290 fix for cloud sessions staying asleep after a container restart lost a pending `/loop` wakeup or scheduled task; Claude is no longer told, and the session stays asleep

release_history.summary: Fixed prompt and agent hooks that failed to block prohibited actions and improved evaluation of instruction-style Stop and SubagentStop hooks.

evidence.excerpt: <Update label="2.1.294" description="October 8, 2026">
Fixed `prompt` and `agent` hooks written as instructions (such as "Block commands that...") allowing what they should block

release_history.summary: Added fail-closed behavior for command and HTTP hooks, terminal program-status support, and additional gateway routing and audit options. Fixed headless text output and MCP reconnection behavior.

evidence.excerpt: <Update label="2.1.295" description="October 8, 2026">
Added `onFailure: "block"` for command and HTTP hooks: a hook that can't start, times out, or exits with an unexpected code blocks the action instead of letting it through

release_history.summary: Added subagent-specific auto-compaction windows and a workflow-agent model override; extended gateway policy to Desktop Code. Also fixed secret-redaction coverage and managed-hook enforcement.

evidence.excerpt: <Update label="2.1.296" description="October 9, 2026">
Added `autoCompactWindow` to subagent frontmatter and `--agents` definitions, so a subagent can auto-compact earlier than the main conversation's window
